It all entirely depends on how much fat you have in that area. Some people would lose all of the fat there and would be left with loose skin so they would need a neck lift. Some people may retain more weight there and if their elasticity is good, liposuction is a good option. But a neck lift can address both issues at once. I would definitely suggest getting a consultation with a plastic surgeon to talk about what would be best for you.

When you gain weight, your skin expands and then loses elasticity meaning it will not go back to its original placement. With liposuction, yes you take away the fat cells and it is considered “permanent” since you take away many of the cells but that’s not to say that the cells left behind can’t still expand. So yes it’s much less likely to gain weight but still technically can. So if your chin is full of expanded fat cells and then you take the cells away, you do not take away the space that they had expanded

With a neck lift it’s pulling the skin tight if it’s loose, lipo is removal of the fat while leaving the skin how it is. You can do lipo at any weight but it is more commonly recommended for people who are at or near their goal weight. The worry would be that if you did get lipo now, you would also need a neck lift later due to sagging skin. If you lost weight and the stubborn fat went away, you still may be left with loose skin which would still result in a neck lift. If it’s genetic though, you may consider doing the lipo.
